newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM asks rebel defectors not to take sides.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM asks rebel defectors not to take sides.

text.p: Cambodian Co-Premier Hun Sen on Monday warned defectors from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement not to take sides between the country's political parties and exacerbate tensions.

A wave of guerrilla defections over recent months has sparked competition between joint prime minsters Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh, each vying to outdo the other in recruiting the former fighters to their side.
The defectors have gained political muscle by taking advantage of the rifts, winning top ranks in the military and key concessions from the government.
Tensions between the two premiers have gone from bad to worse, weakening the fractious coalition government they formed after U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.
Khmer Rouge defectors who chose to align with one party in order to harm another were creating a dangerous situation, Hun Sen said.
"There is no reason to join with someone to fight someone else. When we fight, we only die," Hun Sen said in a speech to former Khmer Rouge fighters that was broadcast on state radio.

The Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 "killing fields" rule left more than one million Cambodians dead from overwork, disease, malnutrition or murder, signed a peace pact in 1991 but later reneged on the deal.
Fewer than 2,000 of the hardline Maoist guerrillas are thought to remain following the defections, which started last August.

Hun Sen's appeal for neutrality came the day before he leaves for a three-day trip to Laos, during which the two neighbours are expected to sign agreements on mine clearance programmes and cross-border telecommunications.
